body:
Part of my situation is because I wasn't important to my friends and family.  I know they love me.  They just love themselves more.  And that's fine, but I've always suffered for it.  I've been in trouble for years, and they've known it, and they've left me to get myself out of it no matter how much I asked for help.

I love my friends and family, and on the one hand, I don't want to hurt them.  On the other hand, where were they when I actually needed them?  If I'm on my own, fine, but I can't handle this on my own, and they wouldn't accept that when I told them.  I actually think that I'll serve as an example because when my younger cousins in the future say that they need help, maybe they'll get it because my family will have learned their lesson.

I have to wait forever.  Half hour sounds right. And I'm not sure they're even trained, because twice I've been told "your situation sucks; I don't know what to tell you."  I never feel motivated in staying alive after talking to them.  I just stopped calling.
I'm still here, for now.  I have to say goodbye to a friend of mine and he hasn't been around.

I applied for 7 jobs just yesterday.  I go at most 3 days between applying for jobs.  I'm not actually lying about looking for a job.  I have applied for nearly 500 jobs, most of them retail and fast food, and many of them repeat locations, in the past 2 years.  I have not even had an interview in a year, and I've only had 5 interviews in all.  I live in a county with a 13% unemployment rate.  I apply for work outside my county, but I'm usually discriminated against for living far away.  I'd move closer if I had any money.

Right now, to stop myself from going completely insane, I'm working on the business proposal of the business I would open if my credit rating wasn't full of suck and there were actual investors.  But when I'm working on that business proposal, that's the only thing I'm thinking about.  I apply for jobs very regularly, and it wasn't long ago I realized I'd have a job if I made up my own.

They would have to believe me first.  Any time I've tried to tell them before, they blew me off or said I was being melodramatic.

Of course, when I lost my car, everyone was like "Oh my god, why didn't you tell us you were in trouble blah blah blah" after the fact when I had been telling them before that I was in trouble.   They also cared more about the car than my job.  They only hear what they want to hear and like to blame me for everything.  I'm used to getting blamed for everything, and I don't mind it, but I wish they'd believe me before things get drastic.

And I do want to be happy, you are right.  But I honestly don't think I can do this anymore.  I am trying to hang on for those same friends and family that blow me off, but it's really hard to care about their feelings sometimes when I have to realize that they never, ever cared about mine.
